A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SCAR and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B. Content can be reliably matched across the changed pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCAR evaluations on ImageNet, MultiGen-20M, and PIE-Bench, plus ablations and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments, ablations, and qualitative results, with revised CLIP-similarity values in Table 3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same compressed semantic prefilling, attention mask, semantic preservation loss, and semantic alignment guidance. No algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet for class-conditioned generation, MultiGen-20M for text-conditioned generation, SEED-Edit-Unsplash for editing training, and PIE-Bench for evaluation. Control conditions and appendix test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative comparisons, including retrained ControlAR* and EditAR on PIE-Bench. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same model configurations, resolutions, training epochs, metrics, and evaluation samples: 50K ImageNet images, 5K MultiGen-20M examples, and 700 PIE-Bench examples. Appendix protocols also match.

E4.justification: Tables 4–7 retain the same compression-strategy, compression-ratio, encoder, and semantic-versus-VQ-prefix analyses. Figures 7–8 retain the same alignment-strength examples, and the remaining appendix visualizations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Under unchanged reported PIE-Bench settings, Table 3 revises SCAR's Whole/Edited CLIP scores from 26.07/25.08 to 25.08/21.88 and ControlAR*'s from 24.07/23.12 to 23.12/21.43. SCAR no longer leads either CLIP column across all listed methods; its Edited advantage over EditAR shrinks from 3.21 to 0.01. These are localized result revisions; other numerical results and qualitative examples match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including the autoregressive factorization, compression definition, and preservation and alignment losses, are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about semantic conditioning, efficiency, compatibility with next-token and next-set models, and advantages over prior AR editing methods. The revised scores do not produce a corresponding revision of these claims.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and result interpretations remain unchanged, including Appendix A's conditioning comparison and Section 4.4/Appendix B.1's discussion of artifacts from excessive alignment strength. Applicability and future-work statements also match.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces an unspecified future code-release promise with a planned release at the AMAP-ML/SCAR GitHub repository. It still describes release as future work. Implementation details, hardware, and hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references to existing citation groups in Section 2.1, including From Scale to Speed, Jasmine, From Editor to Dense Geometry Estimator, and Eevee. The accompanying discussion and SCAR's positioning relative to prior methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Front-matter edits change the corresponding-author designations from Ryan Xu to Yancheng Bai and Lei Sun, and revise the code-release sentence. Scientific prose, section order, and the appendix narrative remain substantively unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 changes bold and underline emphasis alongside its revised scores. Reference expansion reflows the appendices: Table 7 switches columns and Figure 8 moves to the following page. All seven tables and eleven figures are retained without new visual examples.

improvement.justification: v2 introduces a misleading ranking display in Table 3: SCAR's Edited CLIP score remains bold at 21.88 despite InstructPix2Pix's higher 22.20. In v1, the bold SCAR value of 25.08 actually led that column. This modestly weakens reporting accuracy. The specific planned code address and additional citations provide limited documentation benefits, while the methods and supporting analyses remain unchanged.
